alerts.title: John Henry Kirby Mansion
alerts.architect: James Ruskin Bailey (1926-1928 Tudor Revival remodeling)
alerts.severity_label: Confirmed Demolished (Nov 2, 2026) • Graduated to Lost Houston
alerts.headline: Demolished October 30 - November 2, 2026 following City of Houston Project #26090093 (1/2 Plumbing Sewer Disconnect on 2026-10-14 + 2/2 Building Demolition Permit on 2026-10-30) and Texas DSHS Asbestos Abatement Notification #2026005825 (scheduled 10/27/2026 to 11/06/2026).
alerts.preservation_note: Built in 1894 for businessman J. S. Price and purchased by lumber magnate John Henry Kirby in 1896, the 36-room Tudor Revival mansion at 2000 Smith Street achieved its landmark appearance in a 1926-1928 remodeling designed by architect James Ruskin Bailey (1979 Preservation Houston Good Brick Award). Sold September 30, 2026 to OB Texas Properties LLC (Omair Bashir / Smith St C Store LLC for a planned 13,254 SF Brake Time convenience store & gas station, TDLR #TABS2026022839) and replatted as 'Smith Street Plaza' on October 28, 2026 (Clerk File #RP-2026-435651, Map Film Code #716912), the unprotected structure was demolished between Friday, October 30 and Monday, November 2, 2026 under COH Project #26090093 and TX DSHS Notification #2026005825, and has been graduated to the Lost Houston catalog (lost_kirby_mansion_1894).

Waste will be double bagged, labeled and taken to a dumpster held on site until delivered to an approved landfill. 3. - Emissions of asbestos will be controlled by using wet methods, maintaining negative pressure with a manometric reading of at least -0.02 inches inside the containment, using appropriate PPE and hygiene facilities, keeping the debris picked up during abatement, and double bagging waste before removing from the containment.

dshs_notifications.work_description: 1)Description of procedures to be followed in the event that unexpected asbestos is found or previously non-friable asbestos material becomes crumbled, pulverized, or reduced to powder: work will be stopped until an asbestos survey can be performed to confirm or deny the presence of asbestos 2)Description of planned demolition or abatement work, type of material, and method(s) to be used: 800 spot scrapes (approximately 0.25 sqft each) of spray applied fireproofing to be performed throughout building for the installation of new pipes, ducts and conduit. Abatement to be performed in negative pressure enclosures with a two stage decon and remote shower. Fireproofing to be adequately wet prior to removal. All waste to be disposed of as asbestos containing.

1) If unexpected asbestos containing materials are encountered, the work will immediately cease. The area will be misted with water, and the Asbestos Supervisor will notify the owner's and prime contractor's representatives for additional instructions. 2) The regulated asbestos containing material is primarily pipe insulation or other thermal system insulation. Piping consists of insulated piping and mudded elbows and associated fittings. Negative pressure containment and wet removal methods will be used for removal of TSI from piping and surface of a small tank. 3) To prevent migration of asbestos fibers from the work area, glove bags and negative pressure enclosures will be utilized. Poly containmnets will be constructed and poly sheeting will be use to wrap any remaining TSI on piping or small tank. Continuous negative pressure enclosures will be used during abatement activities, and clearance monitoring in the immediate work area will be performed following decontamination of enclosure. Waste will be double bagged, goose-necked, and labeled; the waste will be placed into a dedicated rolloff and manifested/transported to a permitted asbestos waste disposal site.

1) If unexpected asbestos is encountered or previously identified non-friable asbestos containing material becomes friable (crumbled, pulverized, reduced to powder) work will be stopped until an asbestos survey is performed to confirm or deny the presence of asbestos. 2) Planned abatement work will occur in three phases, and includes a total of approximately 300 scrapes of approximately 0.25 sq ft each or 75 sq. ft total of RACM spray applied insulation (fireproofing) removal throughout the building for subsequent installation of hangers for new pipes, ducts, and conduit. This is a Phased Notification: 11/16/2026 - 12/07/2026; 01/18/2027 - 02/03/2027; and 03/08/2027 03/25/2027. 3) Abatement will be performed within a negative pressure enclosure with a twostage decontamination unit and a remote nearby shower. Fireproofing will be adequately wetted prior to removal. All asbestos waste and potentially contaminated materials (e.g., plastic) will be properly bagged, enclosed (double bagged), labeled and managed as asbestos containing waste; waste will subsequently be manifested and transported to a State of Texas approved asbestos waste disposal site.
